explanation: L13/H7 is a contextual entity-anchor head with a strong first-token sink: at each position it either rests on the text's first token (write near its mean, strength at the floor) or commits 0.6-0.98 of its attention to one nearby preceding content word - normally the head noun of the noun phrase 1-4 tokens back - and copies that token's value into the residual (OV copying +0.31), so it rises well above its floor at the first predicate or dependent token that opens after that noun: the finite verb or auxiliary after a subject, a preposition, particle or determiner right after the noun, a possessive 's, a pronoun or complementizer with an antecedent, or the closing comma. The anchor wins when it is an individuated referent - a person, kin or role noun or name (teacher, nurse, judge, hunter, waiter, postman, guard, wife, everyone) or an institution, organization or place (company, ministry, school, council, committee, government, country, city, bank, river), and with change-of-state verbs any such institutional or placeholder subject, plus first-mention indefinites and possessive nominals with a specific referent ('a stray dog', 'that problem', 'the economy's outlook'); it stays at its floor when the only content word in reach is a mass, scenario or abstract-system noun (weather, climate, rain, storm, heat, wind, traffic, music, noise, evidence, information, news, service, situation, economy, market, prices, confidence, system, process), when an institution is the agent of a transitive activity verb (the council approved, the bank closed, the country requires), when an appositive or a coordinated second nominal splits the anchor, when the subject is a concrete artifact or an animal without such a predicate (the violin needed, the engine hummed, the dog barked), and in function-word-only stretches or at positions before any nominal.
